original_text: Implemented in Rel-1 OSR-060 The oneM2M System should support time synchronization with an external clock source.

attribute_scores.rationale: The term 'time synchronization' lacks specific protocol, precision, or drift requirements.
Does not specify which component initiates the synchronization, the supported external clock protocols (e.g., NTP, PTP), or failure handling.
Consistent with global IoT/M2M architecture terminology and standard time management concepts.
Uses the weak modal verb 'should' instead of the mandatory 'shall' and includes legacy implementation reference text at the beginning.
Technically realistic and standard for distributed M2M/IoT systems requiring coordinated time stamps.
Bundles a historical implementation reference statement with the actual requirement.
Hard to verify objectively due to the lack of quantitative precision or protocol details, though technically feasible.

shortcomings.explanation: The requirement uses the non-mandatory modal verb 'should' instead of the mandatory 'shall' required for baseline specifications.
Includes extraneous implementation background information combined within the requirement statement, violating atomicity.

shortcomings.problematic_excerpt: time synchronization with an external clock source
shortcomings.explanation: Fails to specify acceptable time drift limits, protocols (e.g., NTP/PTP), or behavior when the external clock source is unreachable.

layer1.document_understanding_summary: The requirement specifies time synchronization capabilities for the oneM2M system using an external clock source, referencing a previous release/objective (Rel-1 OSR-060) within a global IoT architecture.

evaluations.context_reasoning: The use of 'should' introduces optionality into an architectural capability that may be required for baseline interoperability in global IoT systems. While common in standards bodies to indicate recommended features, from a strict ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 perspective, mandatory requirements must use 'shall'.

In large multi-release partnership standards like oneM2M, parent traceability metadata ('Implemented in Rel-1 OSR-060') is standard practice for backward compatibility and tracking derivation from high-level use case requirements (OSR). It does not impair the functional atomicity of the requirement itself.

evaluations.original_problematic_excerpt: time synchronization with an external clock source
evaluations.context_reasoning: In high-level requirements specifications (TS-0002), overarching architectural capabilities are defined conceptually, while detailed protocol choices (e.g., NTP, PTP) and drift tolerances are delegated to lower-level technical specifications (TS-0001 / TS-0004). Demanding exhaustive protocol parameters at this architectural level is pedantic and misaligned with standards development practices.

retained_defects.explanation: The requirement uses the non-mandatory modal verb 'should' instead of the mandatory 'shall' required for baseline specifications.

discarded_defects.explanation: Includes extraneous implementation background information combined within the requirement statement, violating atomicity.

layer2.reasoning_summary: Evaluated three candidate defects against the oneM2M IoT architecture specification context. DEF-1 was retained because 'should' is non-mandatory for strict baseline requirements, although common in legacy reference texts. DEF-2 and DEF-3 were discarded as false positives; the inclusion of release traceability ('Implemented in Rel-1 OSR-060') is standard metadata management in large-scale partnership standards, and lower-level protocols (such as NTP/PTP) and error handling are appropriately deferred to technical realization specifications rather than high-level architectural requirements.

layer3.original_text: Implemented in Rel-1 OSR-060 The oneM2M System should support time synchronization with an external clock source.
layer3.refined_text: The oneM2M System shall support time synchronization with an external clock source.
changes_made: Replaced the non-mandatory modal verb 'should' with the mandatory modal 'shall' to ensure conformance with requirements engineering standards.
Removed legacy implementation reference text ('Implemented in Rel-1 OSR-060') to maintain normative requirement clarity.
layer3.functional_intent_preservation_rationale: The core functional intent—requiring the oneM2M System to support time synchronization with an external clock source—remains completely unchanged. Only the normative obligation level ('shall' instead of 'should') and introductory text artifacts were modified to resolve the conformance defect.

checks.observations: Successfully replaced the non-mandatory modal verb 'should' with 'shall'.
No vague adjectives or subjective descriptors were introduced.
No specific protocols, APIs, or arbitrary technical details were added.
The core functional intent regarding time synchronization with an external clock source is fully preserved.
Adheres to IEEE 29148 standards using active voice and the mandatory 'shall' requirement.

layer4.critique_and_feedback: The refinement successfully resolves the identified conformance defect by converting the non-mandatory 'should' to the mandatory 'shall'. It also appropriately cleans up the legacy implementation artifact while strictly preserving the original functional scope and avoiding any unwarranted technical assumptions.
